steps: Unpack & check the packet

Unpack the body, check the manual packet (the glass latch tool and wall thermostat stay with the owner) and unbolt the unit from its pallet: 175 lbs., team lift recommended. Decorative fronts aren't included.

• Manual packet (white box): Glass Latch Tool #HA-77-00256 and Wall Thermostat #05-01-00198 (both must leave with the homeowner), Inswool bag #35-01-00239, small coals bag #35-01-00240, large coals bag #35-01-00311 and the owner's manual. Missing parts: contact Mendota Technical Service.
  • Packed inside the firebox: the firebox lining (Red Brick or Milano Tile, by model) and the fiber log set.
  • Not included: decorative fronts, bought separately. A surround kit must be installed to complete the installation (p. 71).
  • Unbolt the body from the wooden pallet. Net weight 175 lbs.; team lift recommended.
  • The dealer or installer obtains building permits and inspection approvals; Mendota may ask for copies to validate warranty coverage (p. 5).
  • Indoor only: fully protected from precipitation and excessive moisture, ambient 32°F to 110°F. Manufactured (mobile) homes: after the first sale of the home, with the unit bolted to the floor and properly grounded (p. 5).
Convert to LP (if needed)

Do it before placing the unit: kit #HA-48-00328 replaces the pressure regulator, both burner orifices (#56 rear, #59 front), the pilot orifice thimble and the thermocouple. Leak test as the final step.

Qualified service agency only. Turn the electrical supply off first; shut the gas off before disconnecting electrical power. Install in a clean environment; a dropped kit or valve can't be guaranteed.

  1. Turn off gas at the appliance service valve if the line is connected.
  2. Remove the 3 screws (¼" flat blade screwdriver) holding the NG pressure regulator to the valve; discard its black rubber gasket and spring.
  3. Fit the LP pressure regulator in the same position and orientation (it mounts only one way) with the same 3 screws. Put identification label (G) on the valve body where it's easily seen.
  4. Remove both burners. Swap the orifice spuds with a ½" deep well socket: rear #65-14-00056 (#56 drill), front #65-14-00059 (#59 drill). Tighten securely.
  5. Pilot (right side of the firebox): hold the base with large vice grips, loosen the hood ¼ turn counterclockwise with a 7/16" open end wrench and remove it. Replace the NG pilot orifice thimble with the LP thimble, thread the hood on finger tight, then tighten the hex base. Always hold the base while turning the hood, to protect the mount bracket.
  6. Replace the thermocouple with the kit's high temperature thermocouple.
  7. Leak test. Verify minimum inlet and outlet pressures, then light the burners: they must light immediately without lifting, and the pilot flames must overlap the propagation ports on both burners.

Attach the kit's labels to the back surface of the listing label plate (p. 41). Orifices by altitude: see Fuel & conversion.
Frame, place & level
Frame to at least 29-1/2" W × 49" H × 14" D with 60" from the fireplace floor to the ceiling. Set the unit on wood, masonry or metal, then level, plumb and secure it to the framing studs.

• Minimum rough framing: width 29-1/2", height 49", depth 14"; unit base to room ceiling 60"; unit base to 8" mantel 47". The height lets the unit slide in with a 90-degree elbow on top.
  • Floor: wood, masonry or metal across the full width and depth. Never directly on carpeting, vinyl or any combustible material other than wood. On a cement slab, plywood underneath helps keep cold from conducting into the room.
  • Once it's in the cavity, add a secondary nailer stud at least 38 inches above the fireplace floor for securing facing materials.
  • Straight-up vertical vent: notch the front-wall top plate for 1" clearance to the pipe; framing members within that 1" go on edge (the 1-1/2" edge).
  • Elevated installs: build a deck and enclosure, keeping at least 60" from the fireplace floor to the ceiling.
  • Chase: build it like the home's outside walls; insulate walls, ceiling, base plate and cantilever floor; vapor and air barriers per regional code; caulk fire stops, gas line holes and other openings with high temperature caulk (or stuff with unfaced insulation).

Hearth pad and finish-depth rules: see Framing & hearth pad.
Install the vent system
Coaxial rigid 4" × 6-5/8", one brand and series, every joint fully twist-locked; no silicone at joints. Wall thimble through any combustible wall; cap right-side up and sealed to the structure.

• Twist-lock: slide the four female-end indentations into the four male-end slots, push fully together, turn about ¼ turn clockwise. Use fixed lengths instead of telescoping sections wherever possible; telescoping sections stay complete assemblies.
  • No silicone sealants anywhere in the vent; stove gasket cement may be used at joints but isn't required. Don't fill air spaces with insulation.
  • Horizontal runs level or ¼" rise per foot toward the termination, never downward. Support every 3 ft.
  • Horizontal termination off a 90° elbow on the unit: elbow centerline 44-9/16" above the fireplace floor, plus ¼" per foot of run. Frame a 9-1/4" wide × 10-1/4" high opening for the mandatory wall thimble (combustible wall 4" to 8" thick); a 9-inch round hole in masonry or other non-combustible walls. Against a 2x4 or 2x6 exterior wall only a 6" horizontal section is needed.
  • Horizontal cap: slide it over the pipe end, screw it tight to the wall and seal with high-quality caulking; never recessed into the wall or siding. Heat shield #AA-11-00458 (or equivalent) with vinyl, wood or other combustible siding.
  • Vertical: plumb bob from ceiling and roof; ceiling fire stop at every floor; attic insulation shield; wall straps every 3 feet; enclose the vent through occupied spaces above the first floor; nail and seal the flashing with roofing over its top edge; storm collar and cap.
  • Ceiling fire stop openings: frame a 9" x 9" opening in the ceiling (p. 56; step 2 on p. 58). In a multi-story vertical install, frame the openings at the second and later floors to 10" x 10" inside dimensions (step 6 on p. 58).

Not above a meter/regulator assembly within 3 feet horizontally of its center-line, within a height of 15 feet. Vertical caps near each other need an 18-gauge or heavier galvanized barrier 6" taller and 3" wider than the caps; two direct vent caps need at least 18" between centerlines. A wood-burning flue within 36": divider plate, or extend that flue 24" above the gas cap.
Gas line, leak test & input check

Run a properly sized line into the left side of the cabinet to the 1/2" N.P.T. female inlet, with a drip leg recommended. Leak test every joint with soap and water or a gas sniffer, then verify orifice sizes and the input rate.

• Size the line from the supply regulator to the factory manual shutoff with the table in Gas supply pressure. CSST flex line with brass-to-brass fittings; never plastic pipe.
  • The inlet is a 1/2" female NPT fitting: supply a ½" NPT male fitting and adapt your line size to it.
  • Factory manual shutoff valve: left side, above the main gas valve (clockwise off, counterclockwise on). Add an external keyed wall- or floor-mounted shutoff where local codes require one.
  • Drip leg / sediment trap recommended in the supply line.
  • Pressure testing the supply piping: above 1/2 psi (3.5 kPa), disconnect the appliance and its main gas valve; at 1/2 psi or less, isolate it by closing its equipment shut-off valve.
  • Leak test all field joints and the factory gas train joints with a gas sniffer or soap and water solution.
  • Verify orifice sizes and gas input rates (meter test in Manifold pressure).
  • Massachusetts: installation by a licensed plumber or gas fitter, and a CO detector in the room (p. 6).
Electrical connection

Wire 120 VAC into the junction box on the right side through its strain relief; the supply must be hot at all times with no switch in it. Join matching colors with the supplied wire nuts and ground to code.

1. Remove the junction box cover plate (two screws) and route the 3-wire end of the house cable through the strain relief in the cover plate.
  2. Strip the house wires and the three color-coded wires in the box and join matching colors with the supplied wire nuts. Braided to braided: strip both at least ½" and twist them together first. Braided to solid copper: strip the solid ½" and the braided ¾", and twist the braided wire around the solid end.
  3. Put the joints in the box and secure the cover plate.

Ground per local codes, or NFPA 70 / CSA C22.1. Replacement wires need the same type and size of insulation as the original. Label all wires before disconnecting them when servicing controls, and verify operation afterwards. Current rating: see Electrical & blowers.
Refractory liner

The one-piece domed liner ships installed but comes out and goes back in during installation. It's fragile: push it firmly against the back wall and fit the Refractory Retainer Bracket before any firing.

• AA-11-00847: Red Chicago Style (Clinker) Brick liner. AA-11-00872: Milano Style Tiled liner.
  • Remove the glass frame with the supplied tool, then the andiron grate (two ¼" Hex #8x1/2 sheet metal screws, ¼" nut driver).
  • Keep the liner's front bottom still, rotate the domed top forward and out, support the dome from inside, then lift and slide it out horizontally. Reinstall in reverse.
  • Push the rear surface firmly against the firebox back wall and attach the Refractory Retainer Bracket (owner's manual packet) in the orientation shown on p. 47. The manual's steps 7 and 8 must be done before firing.

Damage from mishandling or not following these steps isn't covered by the warranty.
First light, logs & millivolts

With the glass removed, light the pilot with the gas cock dial and red piezo button; it must read at least 325 millivolts. Cycle the burners, then install logs and coals with the pilot running and cycle again.

1. Thermostat OFF and gas shut-offs open. Push the gas cock dial in slightly, turn it clockwise to OFF and wait five minutes.
  2. Turn the dial counterclockwise to PILOT, depress it and push the red piezo igniter button; keep it depressed about 1/2 minute after the pilot lights.
  3. Take millivolt readings and gas pressures (below).
  4. Before installing logs, turn the dial to ON. Main burner ON/OFF switch on: burners should light immediately; if the rear burner doesn't, switch the rear burner ON/OFF switch on. Cycle on and off: prompt ignition, flame running smoothly around the burner curves.
  5. With the pilot operating, install logs and coals, then cycle again: prompt ignition, no lifting. Logs give off a strong, acrid odor at first (about 2 hrs.).
  6. Reinstall the glass front and screen; main burner switch ON.

Millivolt tests (p. 88)

A · Complete system: 2 & 3, thermostat closed100MV or more
B · Thermopile output: 1 & 2, opengreater than 325 MV
C · System resistance: 1 & 3, closedless than 2.8 ohms
D · Auto/pilot dropout: 1 & 2, openbetween 120-30 MV

Pilot only (thermostat and main burner OFF): at least 325 millivolts; burner operating (dial ON, thermostat ON): at least 100 millivolts. Adjust the pilot screw on the control to change millivolts and pilot flame; never below 325 millivolts. The pilot flame must overlap the thermocouple tip, the top 3/8" of the thermopile and the burner ignition ports.

Note: p. 88 says the pilot flame must be a minimum of ¾" long on all three branches; p. 51 and pp. 85-87 say at least 1", especially for LP gas (p. 86 adds that it should typically be 1-1/2").

Log set (pp. 62-70)

Logs A through G, large chunk coals (H), small coals (I) and glowing embers (J), on the rear log pins and main ember bed pins. Log placement is shown only as diagrams (pp. 62-69). Small coals ½ inch apart between the firebox front edge and the grate bars, and in front of and behind the front burner; large chunk coals about ¼ inch apart on the front burner, bridging to the main ember bed (B) without plugging ports; don't pack small coals tightly; embers spread lightly, never dense over ports. Logs or coals must not block the pilot or main burner flame.
Air shutters, damper & flame check

Two shutter knobs sit behind the right-side access door (top: front burner, bottom: rear burner). If the flame is too blue after warm-up, close in 1/8" steps until it turns a realistic yellow; set the vent damper after 20 minutes of burn, never fully closed on a horizontal termination.

Note: the lighting checklist on p. 79 gives an air shutter opening of 0" to ⅛" for natural gas and ¼" to fully open for LP gas; p. 80 says that during initial installation the shutter should be set at 1/8" open for natural gas and 1/2" minimum open for L.P. gas.
  • Adjust only with the logs in place, after warm-up. Hook the control end with the glass latch tool and slide it. Very small changes make major changes in flame; try each setting about ½ hr.
  • Soot on the glass: open the shutter fully until sooting stops, burn four to six hours until the deposits burn off, then close in 1/8" increments.
  • LPG: aim for about a 2" high blue base. Yellow starting at the burner surface means the shutter is closed too far and will soot; logs hanging in yellow flame soot easily.
  • Front burner flames also change with how the coals are arranged. Above 5,000' some variation may be required.

Vent damper (p. 61)

Adjustment rod above the glass frame, center of the convection chamber. Judge the flames after 20 minutes of burn. Horizontal termination: never close it completely. Ghosting flames, or soot on LPG units: open it fully and work back in increments. A 1" downward bend shows the plate position; vertical means fully open.

Lighting checklist (p. 79)

  • Pilot lights immediately and lights both burners; burners cycle on/off without delays.
  • Flame stable, not lifting off the burner after 5 minutes. If it lifts, turn off and check every vent joint is twist-locked and leak proof and the cap is right side up.
  • Gas leaks and pressures checked before facing materials go on.

Normal rear flame at maximum after 30 minutes: 1 to 2 inches above the rear log top edge (p. 89).
Surround, barrier & curing
Remove the hearth pad spacer, fit the required surround kit and barrier screen, and run the 3-step curing cycle (Step 1 before wall finishes). Train the owner and complete warranty registration.

1. Remove the hearth pad spacer from the floor plate (two ¼" hex head screws) and discard it.
  2. Lay the top, both legs and bottom face-up; join them with 1/8" X 1" hinge pins and 1/8" ID X 5/32" OD washers; attach the temporary braces.
  3. Thread an 8-32 nut about 1/8" onto each of the three bottom studs, stand the assembly up and slide the studs into the slots in the floor plate's front flange.
  4. Rotate it in: side attachment brackets between the outer skin and the inner heat shield, top center clip under the inner shield. Fit the screws loosely, remove the braces, check the leg gaps, then tighten the three sheet metal screws.

Ashton surround finishes: Gold, Antique Copper, Swedish Nickel, Natural Iron or Black; optional filigree kits or a cast iron overlay go on the surround parts first. The barrier screen must be installed.

Curing (p. 11)

With barrier screen, surround, front or doors installed. Step 1: Manual (Off) thermostat mode, flame Hi, fan Level 3, at least 2 hours, then off to cool. Step 2: Hi with fan Off until odors diminish, about 3 hours. Step 3: still on, fan Level 1. Blowers on in Step 1 keep smoke from staining the wall; Mendota recommends Step 1 before wall finish materials. Smoke will set off smoke alarms; ventilate the home.

Handover (p. 94): tell the owner curing is required and smoke will be emitted; train them on the glass door and decorative front, the barrier screen requirement, the manual shutoff valve (with the glass latch tool) and periodic maintenance; complete warranty registration (checklist, p. 42).

panels.title: Soot on the glass
items: Burner air shutter closed too much → open it fully until sooting stops, then burn four to six hours
Exhaust damper closed too much → open the damper
Log or ember placement → give coals and embers more room for gas and air to mix
Glass door seal compromised → gasket corners can't bulge; replace it if white through the bulb and no longer sticking
Wrong gas pressure or orifice size → service person checks orifices and outlet pressure (3.5" W.C. Nat. Gas; 10" W.C. LP Gas)

panels.title: Slow ignition or lifting flames
items: Logs or coals blocking the pilot or burner flame → reposition them
Vent joints not twist-locked or leaking → lock and seal every joint
Vent cap not right side up → reinstall it
Pilot not impinging on burner and thermopile → check the pilot flame
Flames ghosting off the burners → open the vent damper fully, then work back in increments
Burner won't cycle on/off without delays → don't operate

panels.title: Pilot problems
items: More than ten seconds to light after sparking → check spark rod position and igniter wires for pinched or damaged areas
Pilot went out → wait at least five minutes before relighting; if you still smell gas, stop
Frequent outages or lockouts → find the primary cause; don't assume the ignition control is faulty
Under 325 millivolts with pilot only → adjust the pilot screw on the control
Lockouts at startup in cold weather → leave the pilot running while daily highs stay 50 °F or lower

panels.title: Flame color
items: Too blue after warm-up → close the air shutter in small 1/8" increments
LP flame yellow from the burner surface → shutter closed too far; open it (about a 2" blue base)
Log hanging in yellow flame → soot forms on that log
Front burner flame → re-arrange the coals or adjust the front burner shutter

light.title: Lighting the fireplace
light.html:
Your fireplace has a pilot light, a small flame you light with a push-button igniter. It lights the burners when you switch them on. The gas controls are behind the left-side surround door.

Glass off first. The manual says to always remove the glass before relighting the pilot (see Clean the glass). If the pilot went out, wait at least 5 minutes first.

Light the pilot

  1. Make sure the gas supply shut-off is open and the thermostat is set to OFF.
  2. Push the gas control dial in slightly and turn it clockwise to OFF. It won't go from PILOT to OFF unless pushed in; don't force it.
  3. Wait 5 minutes for any gas to clear. If you smell gas, stop and see Safety & gas smell.
  4. Turn the dial counterclockwise to PILOT.
  5. Press the dial in and push the red igniter button. Once the pilot lights, keep pressing the dial for about half a minute. If the pilot goes out, try again and hold it longer.
  6. Turn the dial to ON.

Then the burners

  1. Put the glass and the screen back on.
  2. Push the main burner ON/OFF switch to on. The burners should light right away. The rear burner has its own ON/OFF switch: if it doesn't light, switch that on.
  3. For a lower flame and less heat, turn the Hi/Lo knob counterclockwise.

Slow to light, or flames still lifting off the burner after 5 minutes? Turn it off and have a qualified installer check it.

off.title: Turning it off
off.html:
To turn the flames off, push the main burner ON/OFF switch to OFF.

Leave the pilot on in winter

The manual requires leaving the pilot running in the winter months, whenever outside daily highs stay at 50°F or lower. It stops heat escaping from your home through the glass, helps the vent draw when the fireplace starts, and helps prevent lockouts.

Shut off the gas completely

  1. Push the main burner ON/OFF switch to OFF.
  2. Turn the gas control dial clockwise to PILOT, then to OFF.
  3. Turn off the manual shut-off valve inside the fireplace. Open the left-side door: the handle is above the main gas valve. Turn it clockwise to shut off the gas, counterclockwise to turn it back on.
  4. If your installer added an outside shut-off valve next to the fireplace, turn that off too.
  5. If the fireplace is going to be serviced, turn off all electric power to it.
Your installer should show you how to work the manual shut-off valve with the glass latch tool. It's on the manual's handover checklist.

sounds.title: Smoke, smells and sounds
sounds.html:
Smoke and odor in the first fires

A new fireplace has to cure. Materials from manufacturing burn off and the paint hardens, so some smoke and odor are normal. Your installer should run the manual's 3-step curing cycle:

  1. Flame on high, blowers at level 3, for at least 2 hours. Then turn it off and let it cool.
  2. Flame on high, blowers off, until the odors fade, about 3 hours.
  3. Leave it on and set the blowers to level 1, the lowest, until any new odors fade.

Open doors and windows. The smoke can set off smoke alarms. Needing more than 10 hours on high isn't unusual, and slight odors can come back on later startups, fading with use. Finishing materials around the fireplace, like adhesives and paints, can also smell when they heat up.

After a long break

If it hasn't run for three months or longer, expect a smell of burnt dust and lint the first time, like your furnace in the fall.

Hot surfaces and ticking

The wall above, the area in front and the hearth can get too hot to touch. That's normal when the clearances are met. Noise from the steel expanding and contracting is normal too.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Clean the glass now and then, and only once it has cooled to room temperature. You can clean the outside with a cleaner as needed. To clean the inside, take the glass frame off.

Take the glass off

  1. Use the glass latch tool that came with your fireplace. Put it in the hole in a spring latch, pull toward you and rotate it 180 degrees to unhook it. There are four latches.
  2. With both hands, tip the top of the glass frame away from the fireplace about 8", then lift it up 1" at an angle and away. Leave the latch hooks turned upside down; it makes refitting easier.

Clean it

Use Kel Kem Polish Plus (part # 65-06-00455) or a similar product. Never use oven cleaner or abrasive cleaners. The odor additives in gas can leave a white film; it comes off if you clean it in time.

Put it back

  1. Set the two tabs on the bottom of the frame into the two slots at the bottom of the firebox, centered left to right.
  2. Tip the frame in until the gasket touches the firebox.
  3. With the tool, pull each latch toward you, rotate it so the hook faces down, and let it hook the frame. Do all four.
Never run the fireplace with the glass removed, cracked or broken, and put back any barrier screen you took off. Don't strike the glass or slam the door. Check the gasket each time the glass comes off.

flames.title: Flames and soot
flames.html:
After 30 minutes or more at full height, a normal rear flame reaches 1 to 2 inches above the top edge of the rear log. That depends on the gas type, the air shutter setting and the venting, so actual heights can be slightly higher or lower.

Your fireplace has air shutters, dampers, coals and embers that can be adjusted for your fuel and venting. A qualified technician should make those adjustments. Contact your installer or Mendota dealer if it doesn't seem to burn right. Improper setup and adjustment aren't covered by the warranty.

Soot

A few small soot spots on the logs are acceptable. Turn the fireplace off right away and tell your Mendota dealer if you see:

  • Soot areas larger than 1"x1" on the logs.
  • A thin black film on the glass.
  • Soot on the outside of your home around the vent cap.
Don't wait. Mendota and its dealers aren't responsible for damage from excessive sooting that wasn't brought to their attention right away.

fan.title: The convection blowers
fan.html:
Two convection blowers come standard. They move warm air into the room. The fireplace is designed to run with the blowers on or off.

  • The speed knob is behind the hinged right-side surround leg. It turns the blowers on and off and sets any speed in between.
  • The delays are normal. The blowers wait about half an hour while the fireplace heats up, and keep running about half an hour as it cools down.
  • Cooler surroundings. Running the blowers helps cool the wall and surfaces around the fireplace.
  • Less heat spread. Turn the blowers down or off. To move heat around more, your furnace blower or a ceiling fan can help too.

The blowers don't run in a power outage. Cleaning lint and dust around them is part of the yearly service.

power.title: Power outages
power.html:
Your fireplace keeps working in a power outage. The manual says the burner still works, and so does the flame height adjustment.

What stops

The two convection blowers run on house power, so they won't run until the power comes back. Normally they help spread the heat and keep the surfaces around the fireplace cooler, so keep children and pets back from the hot surfaces.

Power to the fireplace

The fireplace's 120 V supply is meant to be on at all times, with no switch in it. Before the fireplace is serviced, all electric power to it should be turned off.

safety.title: Safety and gas smell
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Don't light any appliance.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch, including light switches, and don't use any phone in your building.
  • Immediately call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone and follow their instructions.
  • If you can't reach your gas supplier, call the fire department.

Every day

  • The barrier screen must be on whenever the fireplace is running. If it's damaged, replace it with Mendota's barrier for this fireplace.
  • Keep furniture and other objects at least 60" from the barrier screen, and keep things off the front edge of the mantel.
  • Supervise young children closely and never leave them alone in the room with it. Don't put cribs or bassinets near it. A safety gate can keep toddlers and other at-risk people away.
  • Keep clothing, gasoline and other flammables away. Never burn wood or paper in it.
  • In an isolated bedroom, study or similar room, always run it on the thermostat, never in manual mode. Manual mode can make the room dangerously hot.
  • If any part has been under water, don't use it. Mendota requires replacing the whole fireplace.

service.title: Yearly service
service.html:
A qualified installer, service agency or your gas supplier must service the fireplace every year, in the summer or early fall. The fireplace and vent should also be inspected before first use. Under the warranty, yearly maintenance is your responsibility.

What the service includes

  • Cleaning lint and dust from around the controls and blowers, and checking the wiring under the burner.
  • Cleaning the pilot's sensors (thermocouple and thermopile) and spark rod, and vacuuming the pilot and burner ports. Insects can nest there; they're attracted by the odorant in natural gas.
  • Checking the pilot and burner flames.
  • Taking out the logs and coals, cleaning off lint and carbon, and putting them back as instructed.
  • Checking the glass gasket seal, and replacing the gasket if it has turned white and no longer sticks to the glass.
  • Clearing leaves and twigs from the vent cap, and cleaning the glass.

Your part

  • Check the outside vent cap monthly so nothing blocks it.
  • If you see heavy carbon on the logs, turn the fireplace off and call for service.
  • Lint from carpets and bedding can mean more frequent cleaning.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Mendota gives the original purchaser a limited lifetime warranty, as long as the fireplace stays where it was first installed. It can't be transferred. Coverage starts on the date Mendota invoices your installing dealer, and only for new units sold through an authorized Mendota dealer.

Which parts are covered, and for how long, is set out in a table on p. 95 that this guide can't reproduce. The manual says to see your dealer for warranty information.

Making a claim

Report a problem to your Mendota dealer within 30 days, with proof of purchase, the purchase date, model name and serial number. The serial number is on the listing label, which pulls out on a chain or cable.

Note: p. 13 says the listing label is behind the right side hinged surround leg, and p. 84 says it is in the air gap below the bottom edge of the glass door frame.

Not covered, or voids it

  • No permits and inspections, or installation or repairs by someone unqualified.
  • Skipped yearly maintenance, over-firing, or water damage.
  • A removed or altered serial number.
  • Discoloration, minor warping and noises from the steel moving. Those are normal.

Parts you buy after the coverage ends carry a 90-day warranty, parts only, with a receipt.

specInput.title: Input rates
specInput.html:
NG high / low fire27,000 / 6,750 BTUH
LP high / low fire25,000 / 7,000 BTUH
P.4 fireplace efficiency70.0%

Certified to ANSI Z21.88-2019(R2024), tested by Intertek Testing Services. Designed as a supplemental heat source; an alternative primary heat supply is advisable.

Altitude

Above 7,500 ft., understand the need for gas input derating: ask the local gas company whether the gas is already derated, or contact Mendota Technical Service. Orifices change above 2000 ft (Fuel & conversion); verify the input with the meter test (Manifold pressure). When derating, fill in the High-Altitude De-Rating Label from the owner's manual packet and attach it to the back surface of the listing label plate.

Never over-fire or under-fire by changing orifice sizes or adjusting gas pressure above nameplate BTUH. "Backyard" natural gas wells: send gas analysis data sheets to Mendota for orifice sizing before first firing; unpurified gas voids the warranty.

specManifold.title: Manifold pressure & input check
specManifold.html:
Natural gas3.5" WC +/- 1/8"
LP gas10.0" WC +/- 1/8"
Regulators (parts list, p. 91)NG 3.5-1.3"WC (05-02-00289) · LP 10"-3.3"WC (05-02-00315)

Read at the output tap on the main gas valve. The soot chart gives the same outlet pressures: 3.5" W.C. Nat. Gas; 10" W.C. LP Gas (p. 86).

Natural gas input rate check

  1. Verify the orifice sizes (stamped on the orifice body) and the manifold pressure.
  2. Turn off all other appliances and their pilots; note the gas meter reading.
  3. Run 30 minutes on maximum flame, turn off burner and pilot, read the meter again.
  4. Therms used × 100,000 × 2 must be at least 27,000 Btu below 2000 feet, or at least 26,200 Btu above 2000 feet.

Over-firing can permanently damage the firebox; under-firing can cause delayed ignition. Both void the warranty.

specVent.title: Venting
specVent.html:
Coaxial rigid: 4" diameter exhaust and 6-5/8" diameter air inlet with approved vent caps. All UL Listed coaxial rigid 4" X 6-5/8" components and caps are approved; never mix brands or series. No "low profile" caps (exhaust recirculation, ghosting flames). Its own vent only: never into a chimney serving another solid fuel or gas appliance. The approved vent systems page (p. 33) is a diagram.

Master venting chart (p. 53)

V 0 in. (90° elbow at the collar)H max 48"
V 6 in. · 12 in. · 18 in.H max 9'6" · 16' · 16'6"
V 24 in. · 30 in. · 36 in.H max 17' · 17'6" · 18'6"
V 4 ft. - 25 ft.H max 20'
Each additional 90° · each 45° elbow−3' · −1½' of horizontal
Vent system length45 feet max. (straight pipe less than 45 feet)

The chart assumes one 90° elbow in every horizontal run; the 20' maximum allows no more than three 90° elbows (three 90° elbows: 14 ft). Two 45° elbows can replace one 90°, or offset straight off the top of the unit (20' horizontal still allowed if the first vertical after the last 45° is more than 4 feet). On 45° runs one foot of diagonal pipe equals 8-1/2 inches horizontal and 8-1/2 inches vertical. The 45 feet applies with three 90° elbows terminating horizontally, or four terminating vertically.

Note: the Master Venting Chart on p. 53 gives a maximum vertical run of 45 feet, and p. 58 gives a maximum vertical run of 61 ft. from the top of the fireplace.
Note: p. 53-54 and the chart on p. 56 allow the 20' maximum horizontal run with a vertical section of 4 ft. - 25 ft.; the text on p. 56 allows it with vertical sections totaling between 4 feet and 41 feet.

Above 7500 ft., contact Mendota technical service for venting requirements and restrictions.

specClear.html:

Glass edge to adjacent sidewall12 in.
Vent pipe sides · bottom1 in.

Note: p. 15 (printed "3in. (51mm)") and p. 55 give 3" of clearance above horizontal vent runs, and p. 54, 56 and 58 give 2" above horizontal runs. Enclosed discharge elbows get 3" on top (p. 54-55).

Side walls (p. 21)

Combustible side walls, mantel corbels and legs must fall behind a 45-degree line from the side edges of the visible glass unless they're more than 12" away. If an existing wall can't meet 12", add an NFPA approved clearance reduction shield: 20-gauge or heavier steel on 1" standoffs with at least 1" active airspace, top and bottom open, 12" larger than the heat source in each direction (66% reduction); or R-1 rated ceramic or mineral board (50% reduction).

Mantels (p. 22)

Fireplace floor to top air gap: 34". Mantels deeper than 8": rise and run 1:1, so a 12" mantel goes 12" x (1/1) + 5" = 17" above the convection air opening. Non-combustible mantels can go at any height; an existing combustible mantel must fit the mantel profile chart (Figure 3-9, a diagram).

No furniture or combustibles within 60" of the barrier screen. Finishes over the non-combustible zone see around 350° F; paper faced gypsum board (Type X too) and WonderBoard aren't non-combustible.

specFrame.html:

Nominal framing depth is 14" (the manual excepts corner installs and solid granite or marble slab facings). It may stay 14" or shrink with finish thickness:

Finish ½" · ¾" · 1"13 ½" · 13 ¼" · 13"
Finish 1 ¼" · 1 ½"12 ¾" · 12 ½"

Nailer stud at least 38 inches above the fireplace floor. Weight 175 lbs.

Hearth pad

R-1 non-combustible hearth protection is required when the unit sits directly on the floor. Reduce its depth 2" for every 1" the unit is raised; at 6" or more none is required. The floor in front still reaches up to 200 °F and a pad surface as high as 250°F; with carpet, vinyl or laminate in front, raising the unit at least 12" is recommended. No R-1 rating is needed under the unit. Pad layout: Figure 3-10, a diagram (p. 24).

Note: p. 10 says the R-1 hearth pad must be 18" deep, and p. 23 says it must extend a minimum of 12" in front of the fireplace.
Note: p. 12 gives a maximum hearth pad thickness of 1-1/2", and p. 24 says not to build a hearth pad more than 1-1/4" thick, or the decorative fronts can't be installed.

R-1 underlayment boards, 1/2": Micore 160, 300, SB; Rescor 360; Fiberfrax Duraboard LD. Not structural: only under other non-combustible finish. 1" granite is only R .05. The unit ships with a hearth pad spacer that's removed before the surround kit goes on.

specElec.title: Electrical & blowers
specElec.html:
Ratings label (p. 15)120 Volts AC, 1.5 Amps; minimum line voltage 110 Volts AC
Electrical section (p. 36)120 VAC, 2 Amp power source, for the blowers
Blowersdual, 190 CFM (in free air)
Blower partsRH 15-02-00120 · LH 15-02-00121
Note: the ratings page (p. 15) gives the electrical requirement as 120 Volts AC, 1.5 Amps, and p. 36 says the blowers need a 120 VAC, 2 Amp power source.

The supply must be hot at all times, with no switch in it. Junction box with strain relief clamp on the right side; ground per local codes or NFPA 70 / CSA C22.1. Blower rheostat behind the hinged right-side surround leg: on/off and infinitely variable speed. Blowers delay about ½ hour at heat-up and run about ½ hour at cool-down. Blowers sit behind the firebox rear wall: access means removing the liner, logs, burner system, burner airbox and a floor access plate. In a power outage the burner and flame height adjustment still work; the blowers don't.

specFuel.html:
Ships configured for natural gas. For LP, LP Gas Conversion Kit #HA-48-00328 must be ordered and installed by a qualified service agency (see Convert to LP).

Kit contentsmanual pressure regulator, LP pilot orifice thimble, high temp thermocouple, cap orifices #56 (rear burner) and #59 (front burner)

Note: p. 15 (2000-4500 ft) and the input rate verification on p. 41 (above 2000 ft) give orifices of rear #46 / front #52 natural gas and #57 / #60 LP. The high altitude de-rating text on p. 41 gives #43 (rear) / #43 (front) natural gas and #55 (rear) / #55 (front) propane for 2000-4500 ft, and says to see the data plate for additional information.

Orifice size is stamped on the orifice body; check it with drill bit shaft ends. Ask the local gas supplier first: orifices may not need changing if the supply is already adjusted for altitude. Fill in and attach the conversion and altitude labels to the back surface of the listing label plate. Starting air shutter settings by fuel: see Air shutters, damper & flame check.

conflicts.issue: Hearth pad depth: 'An R-1 Rated Hearth Protection Pad, 18" deep' (3.1 warning, p. 10) vs 'must extend a minimum of 12" in front of this fireplace' (Hearth Pad Requirement, p. 23). Both say reduce depth 2" per 1" of raise and none at 6"+; only 12" reaches zero at 6".
Maximum hearth pad thickness: '[1-1/2" Thick Maximum]' (p. 12) vs 'DO NOT build a Hearth pad that is more than 1-1/4" thick' or decorative fronts won't fit (p. 24).
Current rating: '120 Volts AC, 1.5 Amps' (ratings page, p. 15) vs '120 VAC, 2 Amp power source' for the blowers (3.3, p. 36).

Clearance above horizontal vent runs: 3" ('VENT PIPE TOP TO COMBUSTIBLES 3in. (51mm)', p. 15; '3" clearance on top of pipe on horizontal runs', p. 55) vs '2" above horizontal runs' (p. 54, 56, 58). The p. 15 metric (51mm) doesn't match 3 in. either.
Maximum vertical run: 45 feet (Master Venting Chart, p. 53) vs 61 ft. from the top of the fireplace (Vertical Through-the-Roof Venting, p. 58).

Vertical section that allows the 20' maximum horizontal run: 4 ft. - 25 ft. (chart p. 53; text p. 54; the chart on p. 56) vs 'between 4 feet and 41 feet' (text of Vertical Rise Horizontal Termination, p. 56).

2000-4500 ft orifices: rear #46 / front #52 NG and #57 / #60 LP (ratings p. 15; input rate verification p. 41) vs '#43(Rear) and #43(Front)' NG and '#55(Rear) and #55(Front)' propane (High Altitude De-Rating text, p. 41).

Starting air shutter opening: '0" to 1/8" for natural gas or 1/4" to fully open for LP gas' (lighting checklist, p. 79) vs '1/8" open for natural gas and 1/2" minimum open for L.P. gas' (4.14, p. 80).

Minimum pilot flame length: 'a minimum of 3/4" long on all three branches' (6.6, p. 88) vs at least 1" (p. 51 LP conversion; pp. 85-87, 'especially for LP'; p. 86 adds 'typically, it should be 1-1/2" long').

Listing label location: 'behind the right side hinged surround leg', on a chain in the air gap (p. 13) vs 'in the air gap below the bottom edge of the glass door frame', on a cable (FAQ, p. 84); p. 41 calls it the listing label plate in the air gap at the bottom of the fireplace.

Ceiling fire stop opening: 9" x 9" (p. 56; p. 58 step 2) vs '10" x 10" inside dimensions' at the second and subsequent floors (p. 58 step 6). May be intentional (first ceiling vs upper floors) but p. 56 gives 9" x 9" for all ceiling openings.
conflicts.reason: Both figures fit: p. 58 gives a 9" x 9" ceiling opening in step 2 (as p. 56 does) and 10" x 10" inside dimensions for the fire stops at the second and later floors of a multi-story vertical install in step 6. They apply to different floors; the guide now shows both in the vent step without a box.

review.notes: One manual (85-03-01120-P, 100 pp.) for the M27 Chelsea, AA-11-00847 (Red Chicago Style brick liner) and AA-11-00872 (Milano Style tile liner). Ignition is a millivolt standing pilot lit by hand with a red piezo button (gas cock dial OFF/PILOT/ON, main and rear burner ON/OFF switches, Hi/Lo knob, wall thermostat #05-01-00198 in the packet). The handover checklist (p. 94) lists remote, CPI/IPI, accent light, backup battery and thermostatic-mode items marked 'ProFlame units only'; nothing else in the manual describes them for the M27, so they are left out. The parts list (p. 91) includes a Skytech wire harness with switch (10-03-00072) and a 9V alkaline battery (65-06-00987) whose function isn't described; not mentioned in the guide. Owner lighting follows 5.4 (p. 82-83), which is written as first-time lighting with the glass removed; the guide gives the pilot steps, then glass and screen back on (step 11) before the main burner switch (step 12), and leaves the installer's log and meter steps to the install sequence. Figure-only content not transcribed: overall dimensions (Fig. 3-3, p. 17), clearances to appliance body (p. 20), cutting dimensions (p. 29), approved vent systems (p. 33), vent configuration drawings (pp. 57, 59-60), log placement steps (pp. 64-69), mantel profile chart (Fig. 3-9, p. 22), hearth pad guide (Fig. 3-10, p. 24), flame height image (p. 89); the warranty coverage table on p. 95 has no text, so the guide gives no coverage periods. Catalog checks: BTU 27,000/6,750 NG and 25,000/7,000 LP, efficiency 70.0%, 4 x 6-5/8 coaxial vent, 175 lbs., dual blowers standard, mobile home approval and ANSI Z21.88 match (p. 1, 15, 37). Catalog height/width/depth 49/29.5/14 in. equal the manual's minimum rough framing dimensions (p. 15, 18), not stated unit dimensions (only in Fig. 3-3), so not listed as a mismatch but worth checking. Catalog view area 29 3/4" x 37" isn't in the manual text. Catalog efficiency basis 'P.4.1'; manual prints 'P.4 FIREPLACE EFFICIENCY'. Curing steps (p. 11) give fan 'Level 3' / 'Level 1' and 'Manual (Off) thermostat mode', while the blower control is an infinitely variable rheostat (p. 37); the guide quotes the levels as printed. Exterior vent clearances (p. 34) come from a two-column table; the K values (USA 3 feet above if within 10 feet; Canada 6 feet) sit beside the J label in the raw text, and the 'Vinyl surfaces require 24"' line under G was not used. Not flagged as conflicts: hearth-board R-values for Micore (1.27-1.47 on p. 23 vs 1.2-1.4 on p. 25, both above R-1); 'UNIT TOP TO ENCLOSURE CEILING 1-1/2 in. (41 mm)' metric mismatch (p. 15); French cover text says a conversion kit is supplied, English says a certified kit is needed and p. 48 says HA-48-00328 must be ordered; p. 87 says the pilot should light within five to eight seconds of igniter sparks (spark-ignition wording); lighting steps point to the installation checklist on 'pg. 39' (it is p. 42); p. 54 cites 'Figure #14' and p. 56 'Figure 16 on Page 20', neither present. Massachusetts sidewall-vent CO detector rules (2.3, p. 9) reduced to the p. 6 note in the gas step. check_numbers finds every guide number in the manual text. Oct 12 update: the eleven conflict boxes are now reader notes (10 substantive) and the ceiling fire stop entry is not_a_conflict (9" x 9" ceiling opening; 10" x 10" at the second and later floors). Website check (website.json): Natural Gas 6,750 – 27,000 and LP 7,000 – 25,000 BTUH, 'CSA P.4.1 Efficiency' 70% (manual: 'P.4 FIREPLACE EFFICIENCY ..........70.0%', p. 15) and minimum framing front and rear width 29 1/2", depth 14", height 49" match the manual (p. 15, 18); the website's viewing area (29 3/4" x 37") and shape aren't in the manual text. No website differences, so no website notes.
